label: Biomarker
description: Prioritize marker panel quality, reproducibility caveats, and translational plausibility over mechanistic certainty.
intent: Use this when the user cares most about whether a signal could work as a marker, panel, or stratification aid.

sections.heading: Use Case
sections.guidance: State the intended biomarker use case, such as stratification, diagnosis, prognosis, response prediction, or monitoring.

sections.heading: Marker Candidates
sections.guidance: Identify candidate markers or panels and explain why they are being considered. When more than one modality is available, distinguish RNA-only, protein-only, concordant, discordant, and direction-not-comparable evidence; do not present a candidate as clinically validated from differential tables alone.

sections.heading: Panel Behavior
sections.guidance: Describe how the candidate markers behave together, including coherence, redundancy, and separation of signal.

sections.heading: Reproducibility Caveats
sections.guidance: Highlight confounders, missing validation, cross-cohort uncertainty, or technical issues that could weaken the panel.

sections.heading: Translational Plausibility
sections.guidance: Discuss whether the markers are plausible for real-world use, even if the mechanism remains incomplete.

sections.heading: Recommended Validation
sections.guidance: Suggest concrete next studies, datasets, or assay checks needed before making strong biomarker claims.
